effects: No asset of the signer moves. The function burns the ETH that the message passer holds, by creating a Burner contract that self-destructs. Anyone can call it, and it is not payable.
formats.shown: The screen says the call burns ETH left by withdrawals. It has no fields, and none are needed.

effects: The signer sends msg.value of native ETH to the L2ToL1MessagePasser on Blast. A later burn() removes that ETH.
The contract records a withdrawal message: sender = signer, target = _target, value = msg.value, gas limit = _gasLimit, data = _data.
After separate prove and finalize transactions on Ethereum, the L1 OptimismPortal sends the value to _target and calls _data. On L1, msg.sender is the portal and the L2 sender is the signer.
formats.shown: The screen shows a withdrawal of {@.value} ETH to {_target} on Ethereum, notes that the L1 payout can be lower, and shows the min L1 gas and the nested L1 call.

findings.title: initiateWithdrawal intent says 'ETH withdrawal' when the call sends 0 ETH and only relays a message
findings.evidence: descriptor intent "Start ETH withdrawal to Ethereum". Case 3: value 0, target is the Blast L1CrossDomainMessenger, and the nested call queues a 795000 DAI claim. Case 1: value 0, the nested call is approve on USDC. L2ToL1MessagePasser.initiateWithdrawal accepts any msg.value, zero included.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Send message and ETH to Ethereum", or use "Start L2 to L1 withdrawal".

findings.title: initiateWithdrawal nested L1 call is shown as if it came from L2BlastBridge, but on L1 the sender is the signer
findings.evidence: L2ToL1MessagePasser.initiateWithdrawal records sender: msg.sender (the signer). Case 3 shows the nested 'Relay Blast message to L1' with 'Blast Sender: L2BlastBridge' and 'Queue DAI claim ... 795000 DAI'. The descriptor's calldata params give only spender = the L1 portal. Nothing tells the nested screen that the L2 sender is the signer, not the L2 messenger, so the relayed claim may not happen as shown.
findings.fix: Add a line to the interpolatedIntent or the field label saying the L1 call runs from the Blast portal on behalf of the signer, for example label 'L1 Call (sent by portal for you)'.

findings.title: initiateWithdrawal L1 Call shows raw hex when no descriptor exists for the L1 target
findings.evidence: Case 1 'L1 Call' renders as 0x095ea7b3...fffe (approve on USDC on chain 1). Case 2 renders as '0x'. The descriptor field is _data with format calldata, calleePath _target and chainId 1. The call runs as the L1 portal, not as the signer.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can decode it. When the data is empty, the wallet should show 'None'.

findings.title: initiateWithdrawal L1 payout is decided later by the Blast L1 portal, not by this call
findings.evidence: The interpolatedIntent says '...the L1 payout can be lower'. The L2 contract only stores value: msg.value in the withdrawal hash. The final ETH amount on L1 and the prove and finalize steps happen in other transactions.
